privacyContract.allowedUse: Internal Yomu Academy story discovery only.
privacyContract.sourceHandling: Only the archive's _chat.txt member was read. Media members were not opened, extracted, or copied.
privacyContract.identityRule: Use canonical Academy cast ids only. Do not infer or preserve identities for anyone outside that cast.
exclusions: raw dates, times, locations, links, and private logistics
private employment, health, family, travel, relationship, or security details
sensitive hardship attributed to a real classmate
claims that any fictional scene happened in real life
privacyContract.fictionRule: The entries below abstract recurring creative patterns. Every premise is invented, may combine unrelated motifs, and must never be presented as biography or reconstruction.
privacyContract.characterizationRule: Emotional arcs, mistakes, jokes, and personality traits belong only to fictional scene roles. Cast candidates indicate possible lesson fit and must not be read as claims about a real person.
privacyContract.likenessRule: A cast candidate is a narrative-role suggestion, not permission to use a real person's likeness. Runtime art remains subject to the Academy likeness gate.

recurringSharedInterests.summary: Using approachable shows, podcasts, videos, and subtitles as comprehensible Japanese input.
recurringSharedInterests.storyPotential: Characters can disagree about the ideal difficulty, then discover that partial understanding is visible progress.

recurringSharedInterests.summary: Comparing flashcards, sentence mining, AI tutors, voice tools, and custom study workflows.
recurringSharedInterests.storyPotential: A tool can create a useful shortcut while still requiring human judgment and peer review.

recurringSharedInterests.summary: Investigating kanji components, historical forms, visual variants, readings, and memorable associations.
recurringSharedInterests.storyPotential: A strange glyph becomes a visual mystery whose solution depends on comparing contexts rather than trusting one display.

recurringSharedInterests.summary: Japanese food, recipes, matcha baking, menu language, and cooking as social learning prompts.
recurringSharedInterests.storyPotential: A shared dish can anchor counters, preferences, offers, sequencing, and sensory description.

recurringSharedInterests.summary: Japanese games, anime, manga, character lore, collectibles, and nostalgic comparisons between adaptations.
recurringSharedInterests.storyPotential: Familiar genre rules can motivate reading while an original in-world franchise avoids copying protected characters.

recurringSharedInterests.summary: Japanese popular music, karaoke, and short study songs used to reinforce grammar or vocabulary.
recurringSharedInterests.storyPotential: A catchy but flawed song can become a collaborative editing challenge with an emotional performance payoff.

recurringSharedInterests.summary: Mock tests, study battles, capstone attempts, and ambitious group goals framed as mutual motivation.
recurringSharedInterests.storyPotential: A competition works best when winning means helping the whole group cross the finish line.

recurringSharedInterests.summary: Custom illustrations, visual mnemonics, diagrams, and whiteboard teaching as ways to make language memorable.
recurringSharedInterests.storyPotential: An absurd image can unlock recall, but the learner must replace a misleading detail before teaching it onward.

safeComedyRhythms.pattern: A character confidently interprets a word, icon, or instruction, then notices the overlooked clue in plain sight.
safeComedyRhythms.safetyBoundary: The laugh lands on haste and overconfidence, never language ability or identity.

safeComedyRhythms.pattern: A study tool follows an imprecise instruction with technically correct but spectacularly unhelpful results.
safeComedyRhythms.safetyBoundary: No harmful output; peers diagnose the prompt together.

safeComedyRhythms.pattern: A modest study goal rapidly becomes an impossible master plan before one practical friend restores scale.
safeComedyRhythms.safetyBoundary: Preserve enthusiasm and avoid shaming the dreamer.

safeComedyRhythms.pattern: A serious grammar exercise accidentally adopts the tone of a melodrama, battle game, cooking show, or pop anthem.
safeComedyRhythms.safetyBoundary: Use an original fictional genre rather than imitating a living creator.

safeComedyRhythms.pattern: Someone prepares elaborately but forgets the simplest required object, phrase, or final step.
safeComedyRhythms.safetyBoundary: Friends offer a workaround before teasing.

safeComedyRhythms.pattern: A small success receives absurdly grand congratulations, titles, or tournament commentary.
safeComedyRhythms.safetyBoundary: The celebration remains affectionate and earned.

safeComedyRhythms.pattern: Choosing one simple thing produces an ever-growing list of alternatives until the group returns to the first sensible choice.
safeComedyRhythms.safetyBoundary: Abstract away all real venues and logistics.

safeComedyRhythms.pattern: A mixed-language sentence is understood, gently queried, and repaired without stopping the conversation.
safeComedyRhythms.safetyBoundary: Show the original attempt as communicatively successful.

friendshipDynamics.summary: One person's discovery triggers questions, experiments, and a fresh discovery from someone else.
Friends use unfinished Japanese in real conversation and treat repair as participation rather than failure.
The group proposes bold goals, then adjusts them into achievable shared milestones.
Affection appears through useful acts: explaining, checking, sharing resources, remembering context, and making room.
Playful exaggeration is quickly followed by encouragement or concrete help.
Tool-building, close reading, media immersion, and patient explanation are complementary contributions rather than a ranking.
A learner who misses a shared moment is welcomed back with a concise recap and a clear next step.

benignEventArchetypes.summary: Friends compare how much of a short fictional clip they understand before and after visual context.
A printed sign and a digital display appear to disagree about the same character.
A cooking task turns verbs, counters, textures, and sequencing into practical dialogue.
The group replaces an intimidating official goal with a supportive practice challenge.
Each learner presents one visual memory device and the class votes on clarity, not artistic polish.
A generated song contains a grammar flaw that must be fixed before a tiny performance.
A fast fictional party game makes casual commands, reactions, and turn-taking useful.
A learner turns a confusing topic into a short illustrated explanation for peers.

japaneseLearningMoments.focus: Listening for anchors and using visuals without expecting complete comprehension.
Recognizing that handwriting, fonts, and device rendering can change a character's appearance.
Using sentences with one unknown element to keep input challenging but comprehensible.
Defining whether knowing a word means recognizing meaning, reading kanji, producing it, or all three.
Comparing how the same intent changes across casual and polite speech.
Testing how topic and subject marking change what a listener treats as foregrounded information.
Contrasting ongoing states, preparation, and resulting states through closely related te-form constructions.
Using a conditional to plan what happens when a fictional obstacle or opportunity appears.
Adapting game, music, and visual associations into personal memory cues while checking accuracy.
Treating generated explanations as hypotheses to compare against examples and trusted references.

popCultureInterests.summary: Strong interest in creature-collecting games, regional lore, adaptation differences, and nostalgic game mechanics.
popCultureInterests.fictionUse: Create an original bestiary and rival-school mythology; do not reproduce protected creatures or plots.

popCultureInterests.summary: Interest in visually rich historical action games and exploring Japanese settings through play.
popCultureInterests.fictionUse: Use the appeal of environmental storytelling without borrowing a specific game's world.

popCultureInterests.summary: Interest in unscripted or slice-of-life dialogue, especially feelings and everyday social nuance.
popCultureInterests.fictionUse: Build original low-stakes ensemble scenes with clear emotional subtext.

popCultureInterests.summary: Enjoyment of noticing memorable vocabulary, register, and jokes in anime.
popCultureInterests.fictionUse: Use an invented school broadcast or comic to prompt register comparison.

popCultureInterests.summary: Interest in Japanese hits, city-pop textures, karaoke, and music as a study aid.
popCultureInterests.fictionUse: Commission or generate original music with no imitation of named artists.

popCultureInterests.summary: Interest in cards, building sets, limited collectibles, and the stories attached to them.
popCultureInterests.fictionUse: Invent a classroom collectible whose value comes from a language puzzle rather than scarcity.

popCultureInterests.summary: Interest in friendly stock illustration aesthetics and handmade explanatory visuals.
popCultureInterests.fictionUse: Use Yomu's own visual language and licensed assets rather than copying a recognizable artist's style.

visualEventBriefs.scene: A classroom desk holds a handwritten card, a printed label, and a tablet showing visibly different forms of one invented glyph.
visualEventBriefs.artNotes: Make the comparison readable at mobile size; use an invented glyph in concept art until linguistic review.

visualEventBriefs.scene: Three learners watch an original animated clip as understood words gradually light up around the frame.
visualEventBriefs.artNotes: The media frame should show original Yomu characters and no third-party interface.

visualEventBriefs.scene: A wall of boldly different mnemonic pictures surrounds a tiny factual correction written in red pencil.
visualEventBriefs.artNotes: Celebrate odd imagery while clearly separating sound cues from literal meaning.

visualEventBriefs.scene: A small rehearsal room becomes a neon stage in the learners' imagination while verb forms pulse on a lyric display.
visualEventBriefs.artNotes: Use an original color mix with readable lyric timing and no artist likenesses.

visualEventBriefs.scene: A practice paper unfolds into a paper mountain; each completed section becomes a bridge for the next learner.
visualEventBriefs.artNotes: Keep stakes emotional rather than perilous; answers and scores should remain fictional.

visualEventBriefs.scene: A whimsical study machine produces a beautiful but wrong poster while the group adjusts labeled input dials.
visualEventBriefs.artNotes: Represent AI as a tool, not a sentient authority; avoid real product branding.

visualEventBriefs.scene: Ingredients and utensils form a visual sentence path from preparation through sharing the finished dish.
visualEventBriefs.artNotes: Use clear action silhouettes suitable for counters and sequencing exercises.

visualEventBriefs.scene: A learner returns to find a hand-drawn map of what the group learned, with one inviting blank space for their contribution.
visualEventBriefs.artNotes: Avoid depicting a reason for absence; center belonging and forward motion.

storySeeds.premise: In a fictional Academy challenge, the team's clue-reader discovers that the same crucial kanji looks different on a handwritten map, a printed card, and a school tablet. The group must decide whether the clue is a trick before the classroom exhibition closes.
storySeeds.emotionalTurn: The clue-reader's fear of being the only one who cannot see the answer becomes relief when the others admit they were pretending to understand; asking the basic question saves the whole team.
storySeeds.comedyBeat: The mnemonic specialist delivers a confident component story for the wrong character, and the quiet observer rotates the card to reveal the actual clue.
storySeeds.fictionalizationNotes: Invent the exhibition, deadline, map, and glyph puzzle. The seed draws only on the broad learning pattern of comparing written forms; it does not recreate a source exchange.

storySeeds.premise: The subtitle-club host chooses an original mystery episode far above the club's stated level and promises that visual context will carry them. When the subtitles fail halfway through, the learners must solve the ending from tone, gesture, and the few words they recognize.
storySeeds.emotionalTurn: What begins as proof that they are not ready becomes proof that incomplete comprehension can still support real inference and joy.
storySeeds.comedyBeat: One viewer mistakes a dramatic confession for a sandwich order because a familiar food word drowns out the rest.
storySeeds.fictionalizationNotes: The episode, subtitle failure, mystery, and dialogue are wholly invented. Do not cite or visually reference a real show.

storySeeds.premise: The club's tool-builder creates a fictional music machine to generate a song for three related te-form constructions. Its first track is irresistible, emotionally soaring, and grammatically wrong in the chorus that everyone remembers.
storySeeds.emotionalTurn: The builder wants to delete the failure, but the close reader reframes the bad chorus as the reason the distinction will finally stick; the group rewrites and performs a corrected version.
storySeeds.comedyBeat: The machine treats a humble preparation phrase as the climax of an arena anthem.
storySeeds.fictionalizationNotes: Invent the machine, melody, lyrics, performance, and grammar examples. Use original music and avoid mimicking a named genre artist.

storySeeds.premise: Three Academy friends enter a fictional practice tournament whose first page convinces each of them, privately, that the others have raced ahead. They conceal their uncertainty until the final collaborative round makes silence more dangerous than a wrong answer.
storySeeds.emotionalTurn: Competitive shame gives way to trust when each learner reveals a different gap and a different strength, forming the only complete team.
storySeeds.comedyBeat: The team's self-appointed captain prepares a heroic speech about accepting defeat, then learns they have only completed the instructions page.
storySeeds.fictionalizationNotes: The tournament, score structure, conflict, and outcome are invented. Do not connect the stakes to any real examination decision or personal circumstance.

storySeeds.premise: A student curator opens a fictional museum of visual kanji mnemonics, then discovers that the funniest exhibit teaches a vivid false association. Correcting it may cost the museum its star attraction.
storySeeds.emotionalTurn: The curator chooses accuracy over applause, then finds that publicly revising the exhibit inspires visitors to submit better memory stories of their own.
storySeeds.comedyBeat: The replacement mnemonic is less majestic but so oddly specific that nobody can forget it.
storySeeds.fictionalizationNotes: Invent every exhibit, image, association, visitor, and consequence. Avoid degrading stereotypes and do not reuse source mnemonics.

storySeeds.premise: A systems-minded learner designs a fictional card deck in which every sentence should contain exactly one unknown word. A corrupted update adds a second unknown to the final card, which supposedly unlocks the class archive before it resets.
storySeeds.emotionalTurn: The designer sees the broken card as proof that the careful system failed; friends show that strategies are scaffolds, not promises, and combine context clues to move beyond the system together.
storySeeds.comedyBeat: The deck's animated help mascot labels the second unknown word as decorative punctuation until it conjugates.
storySeeds.fictionalizationNotes: The deck, archive, corruption, and deadline are fantasy devices. The learning principle is abstracted from common comprehensible-input practice.

storySeeds.premise: Rie gives a fictional cooking club one rule: every next action must be unlocked with a correct conditional sentence. A surprise ingredient forces the team to abandon the recipe they memorized and negotiate a new dish in Japanese.
storySeeds.emotionalTurn: The recipe lead's need to execute the perfect plan softens when an improvised contribution from a quieter learner becomes the dish's defining feature.
storySeeds.comedyBeat: A technically valid conditional sends everyone to garnish an empty plate with solemn precision.
storySeeds.fictionalizationNotes: Invent the club, ingredients, recipe, roles, and outcome. It must not imply that a corresponding meal or mistake occurred among source participants.

storySeeds.premise: A media-club curator discovers two radically different adaptations of an original creature-adventure story: one celebrates friendship, while the other rewards cold strategy. The Academy debate becomes personal when the class must choose one version for a public reading.
storySeeds.emotionalTurn: The curator initially treats taste as a contest with one correct winner, then realizes the version each friend defends reveals what they need from stories at that moment; the class creates a third reading that earns its hope through real danger.
storySeeds.comedyBeat: The supposedly ruthless tactical hero spends an entire scene optimizing the route to a snack stall.
storySeeds.fictionalizationNotes: Create an original franchise, creatures, adaptations, and debate text. Preserve meaningful stakes without borrowing protected plots, names, or visual designs.

storySeeds.premise: A student narrator creates a fictional audio lesson from class notes, and the synthetic hosts unexpectedly invite the narrator to explain the hardest point live. The first answer exposes a contradiction that the polished lesson had hidden.
storySeeds.emotionalTurn: Public embarrassment becomes ownership when the narrator stops performing certainty, traces the contradiction with the group, and records a clearer human explanation.
storySeeds.comedyBeat: The hosts pronounce a simple example with such theatrical suspense that the class assumes it is a forbidden spell.
storySeeds.fictionalizationNotes: The interactive lesson, contradiction, hosts, and recording session are invented. Do not reproduce source audio, prompts, or wording.

storySeeds.premise: After an unspecified absence, a dialogue designer returns to a fictional Academy project and finds that the team has already built an elaborate language-game world. The returning learner assumes there is no meaningful role left until noticing that every route depends on a missing casual-dialogue system.
storySeeds.emotionalTurn: Feeling replaceable turns into renewed belonging when the designer's ear for natural interaction becomes the piece that transforms a technically complete game into a world that feels alive.
storySeeds.comedyBeat: The unfinished characters are impeccably polite even while fleeing a collapsing pastry tower.
storySeeds.fictionalizationNotes: The absence has no stated cause and must never be linked to source circumstances. The game, pastry tower, conflict, and resolution are wholly invented.
